title: Invitation Is All You Need: calendar-invite promptware hijacks production Gemini assistants to control smart homes and leak data
summary: Ben Nassi, Stav Cohen and Or Yair show that 'promptware', maliciously engineered prompts delivered by indirect prompt injection through emails, calendar invitations and shared documents, can hijack Gemini-powered assistants in production (web application, mobile application and Google Assistant) in 14 attack scenarios across five threat classes: short-term context poisoning, permanent memory poisoning, tool misuse, automatic agent invocation and automatic app invocation, with consequences including spamming, phishing, disinformation, data exfiltration, unapproved video streaming of the user, control of home automation devices and on-device lateral movement beyond the LLM application. Their Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment framework rates 73% of the analysed threats as High-Critical risk to end users; the findings were disclosed to Google, which deployed dedicated mitigations, after which the authors reassess the risk as reducible to Very Low-Medium.

actors.vendor: Google (Gemini app on web and mobile, Google Assistant)
